quotes.quote: This policy outlines how TrendAI™ Zero Day Initiative™ (ZDI) handles responsible vulnerability disclosure to product vendors, TrendAI™ customers, security vendors, and the general public.
TrendAI™ ZDI may issue a public advisory disclosing its findings fifteen business days after the initial contact.
TrendAI™ ZDI will allow the vendor four months (120 days) to address the vulnerability with a security patch or other corrective measure
if a vendor is not responsive or unable to provide a reasonable statement as to why the vulnerability is not fixed
TrendAI™ ZDI will publish a limited advisory including mitigation in an effort to enable the defensive community to protect the user.
Extensions to the 120-day disclosure timeline are up to the sole discretion of TrendAI™ ZDI and will be granted only in rare circumstances.
For critical-rated bugs where active exploitation is detected or imminent, the vendor will have 30 days
vendors will be given a disclosure window of 60 days
All other reports in this category will be given a time of 90 days.
In no cases will an acquired vulnerability be "kept quiet" because a product vendor does not wish to address it.
Repository security advisories allow maintainers of public repositories to privately discuss and fix a security vulnerability in a project.
Privately collaborate to fix the vulnerability in a temporary private fork.
You can give credit to individuals who contributed to a security advisory.
GitHub is a CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) and is authorized to assign CVE identification numbers.
GitHub usually reviews the request within 72 hours.
Requesting a CVE identification number doesn't make your security advisory public.
GitHub cannot assign CVEs to your project if it is covered by another CNA.
Anyone can see the current version of the advisory data, as well as any advisory credits that the credited users have accepted.
you should add a fix version to a security advisory prior to publishing the advisory
Imminently available, and you are able to, wait to disclose the issue when the fix is ready.
In development but not yet available, mention this in the advisory, and edit the advisory later, after publication.
Not planned, be clear about it in the advisory so that your users don't contact you to ask when a fix will be made.
